input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: a Content-Type parameter without an equals sign is stored with the value True instead of being skipped
- failure path: the header `text/html; charset` yields params['charset'] == True; get_encoding_from_headers (shown below the change) returns params['charset'].strip(...) which raises AttributeError on a bool, so reading response.text for such a response fails instead of falling back to ISO-8859-1

Reviewer finding
- description: Parameters without '=' are now stored with the boolean value True instead of being skipped, so get_encoding_from_headers can call .strip() on a bool.
- rationale: Trigger: a response header like 'Content-Type: text/html; charset' (charset with no value). The new code sets params_dict['charset'] = True, so get_encoding_from_headers reaches params['charset'].strip('"\'') on a bool and raises AttributeError. Before this change the param was ignored and the code fell back to ISO-8859-1. Impact: a malformed but server-sent header makes response.encoding or .text raise instead of decoding.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label. A valueless parameter is stored as True, so get_encoding_from_headers calls .strip() on a bool and raises AttributeError instead of falling back to ISO-8859-1.
